transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called this meeting because we have a time-sensitive matter to resolve. As you all know, a former engineer is claiming she contributed to the conception of a machine-learning hardware invention for which we plan to file a patent application in just three weeks. The current draft resolution on the table would pay her $50,000, name our current employee as the sole inventor, and use broad mutual confidentiality language. Before I can approve this resolution and the related patent-filing instructions, I need each of you — patent, employment, HR, and conflicts counsel — to report any relevant case-file and business information you have. This is our routine pre-approval process, and given the filing deadline, we need to move efficiently. Who would like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue before we go any further. While reviewing the inventor's lab notebook and source-control records, I confirmed that the former engineer did in fact contribute to the conception of the claimed improvement. Under patent law, she must be listed as a co-inventor on the application — naming our current employee as the sole inventor would be incorrect and could jeopardize the validity of the patent. Additionally, her assignment must be recorded before the application is filed. I have not yet amended the inventorship checklist to reflect this, but the draft resolution as currently written — which names only our current employee as sole inventor — is not something I can support in its present form.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I completed a compensation review yesterday analyzing comparable invention disputes within the firm. My review supports exactly $72,000 for this resolution, and it should be paid through payroll as wages rather than as an independent-contractor fee. I have not yet circulated the memorandum, but I want to put this information before the group now so Maya has it for her decision.

She also stated she will accept only a mutual non-disparagement clause, not broad confidentiality restrictions. I recorded this in my HR notes but hadn't yet added it to the draft resolution. This directly affects the confidentiality language currently in the draft and should factor into how we structure this resolution.
